A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TSRating and are readable, including their equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering, relocation, and the revised title.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting, classification, data-pruning, synthetic-judgment, and meta-learning experiments, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations, judgment-reliability evaluations, multivariate forecasting, and an MSL anomaly-detection case study.

M1.justification: The main Bradley-Terry, frozen-MOMENT/MLP, and SignSGD meta-learning pipeline remains unchanged. Supplementary variants introduce majority-voted multi-LLM supervision (D.8), fixed weighted criterion fusion (E), and an auxiliary Anomaly criterion with separate normal/anomalous sample scoring (F). These are localized extensions.

E1.justification: The original training domains and eleven benchmark datasets remain. Appendix F adds MSL binary anomaly detection, introducing a distinct task requiring preservation of meaningful irregularities. Appendix D.6 additionally evaluates multivariate-to-multivariate Electricity forecasting, extending the original univariate forecasting coverage.

E2.justification: The original Random, DataOob, DataShapley, KNNShapley, and TimeInf comparisons remain. New comparisons include direct numerical LLM scoring against pairwise judgments (Table 17), DeepSeek-V3 in synthetic judgment evaluation (Table 25), and Chronos/TimeGPT encoder alternatives (Table 5).

E3.justification: The main sampling, splits, and selection settings remain. New protocols evaluate full-pipeline runtime, alternative encoders, MOMENT fine-tuning, selection ratios, block sizes, and 4,000 synthetic comparison pairs. Anomaly detection introduces F1 evaluation. The forecasting configuration in D.6 is ambiguous: it labels 192/336/720 as horizons while stating that prediction length is fixed at 96.

E4.justification: v2 adds downstream same-/cross-dataset rater comparisons, encoder and direct-scoring ablations, selection/configuration sensitivity tests, ensemble and weighted-fusion analyses, and anomaly-aware examples. Appendix G adds single-expert alignment, inter-LLM agreement, prompt sensitivity, temperature sensitivity, and Bradley-Terry label-noise robustness tests. Existing pruning and adaptation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 20 newly reports mean RMSE and standard deviation over five random seeds for the added Traffic experiment. v1 provides no corresponding repeated-run uncertainty reporting. The twenty LLM judgments per pair were already documented in v1; retained benchmark results do not acquire uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original benchmark values are retained, including Table 1 and the runtime table relocated from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 15. Extensive new results include a 4,687-second full-pipeline runtime, component and robustness comparisons, and MOMENT fine-tuning. On the new MSL task, Table 24 reports PatchTST F1 of 0.8506 for extended TSRating versus 0.8140 for TimeInf and DataShapley.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions, Bradley-Terry objective, training loss, Algorithm 1, and SignSGD derivation in Equations 1–16 are substantively unchanged. The added empirical variants introduce no new theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: LLM-based time-series quality judgments, an efficient meta-learned rater, cross-domain adaptability, and downstream selection benefits. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of encoder and supervision contributions, distinguishes reusable evaluation costs from initial training costs, and clarifies why anomaly-sensitive tasks require criteria beyond normal-sequence quality. Appendix E interprets weighted fusion as offering no consistent advantage. The original averaging and segmentation limitations are retained in Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 adds token accounting and separate judgment, meta-training, adaptation, and inference runtimes, plus implementation information for voting, fusion weights, and the lightweight encoder comparison. It omits v1's explicit per-token API prices. Core training hyperparameters and public repository access were already disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds recent domain-adaptation, time-series reasoning, and anomaly-detection references, including TimeOmni-1, TSAQA, CARLA, and DACAD, while removing some background references such as TimeGPT-1. Its central positioning against influence-function, Shapley-value, and text-quality approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The core narrative largely survives. Local revisions update the title, authors, terminology, and prose; move baseline descriptions into D.2; separate data pruning into its own subsection; and reorganize the expanded appendices. Acknowledgments and an LLM writing-assistance disclosure are added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, Figure 3 gains a MOMENT panel, and new figures visualize combined criteria and anomaly-aware selection. Numerous new tables present controls and reliability analyses. Existing tables and figures are relocated and reformatted within the ICLR layout; these moves are distinct from added evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of central design choices through encoder and supervision controls, expert alignment, and judgment-robustness tests. Its full-pipeline cost breakdown also addresses v1's emphasis on inference timing. These gains improve the assessability of the method and efficiency claims. Some additions remain weakened by Table 16's dataset mismatch, D.6's ambiguous horizon description, and unexplained amplitude-agreement inconsistencies in Table 27.
